history.dynasty: Badami Chalukyas (main group); Kalyani Chalukyas (later additions)
history.summary: CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KARNATAKA (town Badami), not the value shown in the CSV. Sandstone temple group on the east bank of Agastya lake in Badami (ancient Vatapi), opposite the rock-cut cave temples. Two subgroups: the East Bhutanatha (main) group in Dravida style, 7th-8th century, built in two stages - inner shrine and gudha-mandapa in Badami Chalukya style (massive pillars, Ganga and Yamuna flanking the shrine doorway), outer mantapa added in the 11th century under the Kalyani Chalukyas; and the North Bhutanatha (Mallikarjuna) group, 11th-12th century, in Nagara style. The main shrine holds a Shiva linga. ASI-protected site; occasional rituals still performed by local devotees.

name: Bhutanatha Temple
town_description: Badami (ancient Vatapi) was the capital of the Badami Chalukya dynasty (6th-8th century) in Bagalkot district, Karnataka. Set among red sandstone cliffs around Agastya lake, it holds the famous rock-cut cave temples, fort walls, and several early structural temples; Aihole and Pattadakal lie nearby, forming the Chalukyan architectural triangle.

travel.road: On the east bank of Agastya lake; about a 10-minute walk through old-town lanes from the Badami Museum; auto-rickshaws available

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; sunsets over the lake are celebrated
